name: PrivateFirewall
tagline: A live control plane and intrusion-alert dashboard on top of your OS's own firewall (ufw / Windows Firewall) — kill switch, default-deny, connection monitor.
description: PrivateFirewall is a user-mode control plane and monitoring dashboard layered on the firewall your OS already enforces in the kernel — ufw/netfilter on Linux, the Windows Filtering Platform on Linux (Quick OS / Ubuntu). It shows a live view of every active connection, throughput and listening port; provides a kill switch and dynamic block/allow rules (per-application on Windows, per-port/profile on Linux — mapped honestly per platform); zero-trust default-deny-outbound lockdown; and an intrusion/anomaly alert engine (port scans, brute-force, new listeners, plaintext-DNS bypass, host fan-out, upload surges) with time-boxed auto-blocking. Local-network background chatter is classified as noise, never as attacks, and desktop notifications are strictly opt-in. Fail-open by design: the kernel keeps enforcing policy even if the engine stops, and on Linux the privileged helper refuses to disable ufw at all. Pure Python standard library plus PowerShell/ufw — no drivers, nothing leaves your machine. In-app Help (F1) documents both platforms and their differences.
aiStack: Python (stdlib; ctypes over WFP/iphlpapi on Windows, ufw + /proc + polkit helper on Linux), PowerShell, single-page HTML/JS dashboard
